subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: The Word 'Robot': A Czech Invention
description: One-minute skill: The Word 'Robot': A Czech Invention.

hook.text: The word robot comes from a 1920 Czech play. Karel Capek coined it from 'robota' — meaning forced labor.

buildup.text: In Capek's play R.U.R., artificial workers are created to serve humans. They eventually rebel and take over.

discovery.text: The play introduced the idea that machines might replace human workers — and the fear that comes with it.

twist.text: Capek's robots were biological, not mechanical. They were grown in vats, closer to clones than to machines.

climax.text: The word stuck. Within a decade, robot meant any autonomous machine. Capek gave the concept its global name.

punchline.text: A playwright named the future. Engineers built it.

quiz.question: What does the Czech word 'robota' mean?
options: Iron worker — a person who works with metal
Forced labor — compulsory work or servitude
Clever machine — a device that mimics human action
